themes_detail.label: Graffiti surge in Sunset Park
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 30 THIS WEEK, a 264% increase versus the 8-week baseline average of 8.2 per week (z-score: 4.75), signaling either a coordinated tagging campaign or deteriorating maintenance enforcement in the neighborhood.
evidence: 30 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 8.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Complements existing Streetsblog coverage on neighborhood safety concerns (Sunset Park To Mamdani piece, May 5)
reporting_angles: Are specific corridors or commercial strips being targeted? Map the complaints geographically.
Is Parks Dept. maintaining removal response times? Check turnaround data from 311 follow-ups.

themes_detail.label: Commercial noise complaints triple
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints jumped to 31 THIS WEEK, a 164% spike from the 8-week baseline of 11.8 per week (z-score: 3.64), suggesting new late-night venues, increased foot traffic, or enforcement lapses in entertainment zones.
evidence: 31 noise-commercial complaints THIS WEEK vs. 11.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Aligns with recent labor town hall activity and neighborhood development (Prospect Farm, ULURP in public review)
reporting_angles: Are new food vendors or bars opening without proper permits? Cross-reference mobile food vendor spike (2300% up THIS WEEK).
Which blocks or avenues are hotspots? Interview residents in affected areas near Fourth Ave or Third Ave (per Streetsblog's safety focus).

themes_detail.label: Mobile food vendor complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK, a 2300% increase versus the 8-week baseline of 0.1 per week (z-score: 8.69), indicating either aggressive unlicensed vendor activity or heightened resident complaints about sidewalk obstruction and hygiene.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
2300% spike with z-score of 8.69 (extreme statistical significance)
Converges with commercial noise complaints spike, suggesting general disorder in commercial/vendor zones
reporting_angles: Are these licensed or unlicensed vendors? Request DOH inspection data and FDNY permit records.
Where are they concentrated? Map complaints and conduct street observations in high-traffic areas (Fourth Ave, shopping districts).

themes_detail.label: Drug activity complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints surged to 6 TWO WEEKS AGO (from 0.4 weekly baseline over 8 weeks), a 1500% spike (z-score: 11.62), marking the highest-severity statistical anomaly in the dataset and suggesting either active open-air dealing or a shift in enforcement visibility.
evidence: 6 drug activity complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
1500% spike with z-score of 11.62 (highest severity flag in dataset)
Echoes Streetsblog narrative on neighborhood safety and Third Avenue corridor concerns
reporting_angles: Which blocks or intersections? Request NYPD CompStat data and cross-reference with arrest records.
Has NYPD's 76th Precinct deployment changed, or are residents newly reporting? Interview precinct leadership and community advocates.

themes_detail.label: Heating/boiler complaints persist
themes_detail.summary: Boiler complaints hit 3 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1100% spike from the 8-week baseline of 0.2 per week (z-score: 6.35), while heat/hot water remains the second-largest 311 complaint category overall at 791 over 90 days—a sustained housing quality crisis in the district.
evidence: 3 boiler complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike)
Heat/hot water is 2nd-largest complaint category overall: 791 complaints over 90 days
Converges with budget requests for public housing renovation (NYCHA developments repeatedly underfunded)
reporting_angles: Which buildings or landlords are repeat offenders? FOIL HPD violation records and connect to chronic non-compliance.
Are winter repairs being deferred into spring? Interview residents and tenant advocates on what's causing the spike this late in season.
